violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Sliced tomatoes (51F), shredded cheese (51F), sliced cheese (50F), cooked shrimp (52F) in the 3DR prep top cooler were all not temping properly at time of inspection. Carrot cake (62F) in the desert cooler was not temping properly at the time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD HOLDING FOODS MUST BE COLD HELD AT 41F OR BELOW. PIC TOLD EHS THEY HAD JUST RESTOCKED THE 3DR PREP TOP UNIT AND THE DESSERT COOLER AFTER THE LUNCH RUSH AND FOOD HAD ONLY BEEN IN THE 3DR PREP TOP AND DESERT COOLER FOR 30 MINS. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE ALL FOODS IMPROPERLY COLD HOLDING TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO COOL DOWN TO 41F OR BELOW.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: Serving spoons being held in water with no temperature control. The water the spoons were being held in were temping at 58F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL IN-USE UTENSILS MUST BE HELD IN WATER TEMPING AT 135F OR HIGHER. PIC REMOVED THE SERVING SPOONS FROM THE WATER AT TIME OF INSPECTION AND PUT THEM IN THE 3 VAT SINK TO BE PROPERLY WASHED, RINSED AND SANITIZED.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: The 3DR prep top unit (47F) and the desert cooler (59F) were not working properly at the time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD HOLDING UNITS MUST HAVE AND MAINTAIN A TEMPERATURE OF 41F OR BELOW AT ALL TIMES. PIC CALLED A TECHNICIAN TO COME AND LOOK AT UNITS AND TO FIX THEM AT TIME OF INSPECTION. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT THEY WILL RETURN IN 2 WEEKS TO COMPLETE A FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION AND MAKE SURE UNITS ARE FIXED AND WORKING PROPERLY. Super Chicken (Inspection Date: 08/12/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: EHS observed two batches of cooked yuca sitting on a storage shelf. The cooked yuca had been placed there an hour prior and was temping at 77 degrees.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT COOKED FOOD CANNOT BE STORED FOR EXTENDED PERIODS OF TIME IN AMBIENT AIR ONCE IT HAS BECOME 135F AFTER COOKING. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT HOT FOODS NEED TO BE COOLED FROM 135F-70F IN TWO HOURS AND THEN TO 41 IN 4 HOURS TO PROPERLY COOL. PIC HREW AWAY ONE BATCH OF YUCA AND PUT THE OTHER IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO RAPIDLY COOL TO 70F, WITHIN ONE HOUR.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Boiled yuca was being stored on the ground underneath a shelving unit.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PIC UNDERSTANDS FOOD CANNOT BE STORED ON THE GROUND AND MUST BE 6 INCHES OFF THE GROUND. PIC THREW YUCA AWAY. Super Chicken (Inspection Date: 02/21/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Food Storage No Contamination
violations.observation: Food stored in a location where it is subject to splash, dust or other contamination as follows: yuca being stored on a shelving unit where dirty aprons were being hung up. The apron cords were in the yuca container and touching the yuca. Raw chicken residue was found on one of the aprons touching the yuca.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT FOOD MUST NOT BE STORED WHERE DIRTY APRONS CAN TOUCH THE FOOD AND SHOULD NOT BE KEPT IN AN AREA WHERE EMPLOYEES KEEP PERSONAL GOODS, DUE TO THE RISK OF POTENTIAL CONTAMINATION. PIC THREW YUCA AWAY AND PLACED APRONS IN A DIRTY APRON CONTAINER.
